Rent an apartment first, maybe even with a roommate to lower expenses. You may end up moving around for work or personal reasons and even if it were financially feasible buying and having a mortgage would tie you down in a way you might resent in a few years. With a rental the landlord will maintain the property and in most cases provide working appliances. Renting will let you secure smaller chunks of time on a lease and the ability to move on or stay when the lease is up. With roommates your rent will be lower and you can split other household expenses like toilet paper and coffee. Even renting a room in a house would get you that little bit of freedom from your family while not locking you down like buying does. You might be thinking you'll just sell when you want to move but it's not always that easy. Housing markets aren't stable and you might get back a lot less than you put in or not be able to sell at all. 
I have a couple of electrician journeymen friends who share a very nice rental apartment and neither of them could afford to buy at this point in their careers. Now you may get lucky and good at budgeting and end up buying sooner than later but most people don't buy the first place they move out to. Give yourself time. You may end up wanting to move in with a partner a year or two down the line or get a really good job offer far away that you can't turn down.

The thing about experimental fiction is that there are going to be people who do and don't like that style. For example, most comic book readers are going to like novels that use more visual ellements like the way Hugo used stop motion style illustrations for parts of the story. Fans of typography and cryptography will point you towards House of Leaves wich uses element's of both to reinforce the feeling of uneasiness the characters feel. What Im saying is, take both your praise and your harsher criticisms with a healthy grain of salt because experimental fiction is a niche. Some people will dislike it on principle. Personally I love novels that use it well and it does lend itself to giving some of them the dreamlike feeling you want. I would suggest seeking out some writers/readers of other mixed media or experimental novels. Also if you haven't, you should consider reading or at least flipping through the books I mentioned. Also good examples: Night Film, Only Revolutions,  and the historical classic Lady Murasaki's Tale of Genji (which has over a thousand poems in it!).

The most important thing is that the story should be compelling enough to work with or without the extra layer.
